- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) and forecast is flat or rising slowly, model tends to underreact — correct by adding 2–5% to forecast for next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.3) after a spike, model often overcorrects — reduce forecast by 3–8% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day avg), model frequently overshoots — cap forecast at +5% above peak for next 3 days.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.7) and price is trending upward, model often underestimates — add 1–3% to forecast for next 7 days.  
- When sentiment is volatile (rapid swings) and forecast is smooth, model misses momentum — adjust forecast to match sentiment volatility (e.g., if sentiment drops 0.2/day, forecast should drop 0.5–1.0/day).  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates mean reversion — reduce forecast by 1–3% if sentiment is weak or negative.  
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤ 0.2) over 5+ days, model tends to ignore downward pressure — reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 7 days.  
- If forecast is rising steadily and sentiment is flat or slightly negative, model often overestimates — cap forecast at +2% above current level for next 5 days.
